story: South Africa welcomed more than one million international tourists in October, a rise of about 10 percent that puts the country on course to beat last year’s annual record.
title: Neighbour visits lift South Africa past a million tourists
dek: October arrivals topped one million, up 10 percent, and the rise was driven by visitors from neighbouring countries rather than long-haul travel.
body:
South Africa welcomed 1,020,249 international tourists in October, 10 percent more than a year earlier, Statistics South Africa reported this week. From January to October the count reached 9,437,084, up 10.2 percent. Tourism Minister Patricia de Lille said the country is well placed to pass the record of about 10.5 million arrivals in 2025.

November and December last year brought about 1.9 million tourists between them. Repeat that, and 2026 would finish above 11 million. Missing the record would take a sharp drop, and the monthly series shows no such turn. The November release is due on 17 December. The count comes from border records, and Stats SA says some smaller ports still have gaps because of weak network coverage.

## Who is actually arriving

The growth is real, and it is mostly regional. Three in four October tourists came from Southern African Development Community countries, led by Mozambique (212,875), Zimbabwe (206,581) and Lesotho (166,630). Nearly all of them came by road. Lebombo, on the Mozambique border, recorded 215,299 tourist entries on its own.

Overseas visitors, the long-haul travellers the word tourist usually suggests, numbered 236,375. That was 23 percent of the total, and 0.9 percent fewer than in October 2025. For the year so far, overseas arrivals are up 3.2 percent, to about 1.97 million. African arrivals are up 12.3 percent. They account for most of the extra visitors.

Stats SA's holiday label needs a footnote. It covers 97.8 percent of October tourists, but it includes family visits, shopping and weddings, not only vacations. A million arrivals is not a million people on safari. Most of the million, in fact, never needed a boarding pass.

## A photo finish overseas

In October the United Kingdom sent 39,184 tourists and moved ahead of the United States, which sent 29,583, down 9.6 percent. Germany was close behind Britain, on 37,270. For the year to date the UK is only just ahead of the US: a photo finish, not a changing of the guard. Germany is growing faster than either, up 11.9 percent. Asia is down 13.3 percent for the year, including sharp falls from India and China. Switzerland, ninth among overseas markets in October, sent 6,652 people, up 10.8 percent, and is up 12.9 percent for the year.

A headcount is not a spending figure. The latest full tourism account, for 2024, put the sector at 4.9 percent of GDP and just under 954,000 direct jobs. Domestic travellers supplied most of the money. Foreign arrivals still bring currency, but a border shopping trip and a fortnight in the Cape are not the same economic event. De Lille's statement treats the next job as spreading that benefit, which is a hope, not yet a measured result.

A Wanderlust reader poll also named South Africa the most desirable nature and wildlife destination. That is a reputation vote. The border count is the harder one, and the recovery it shows is still carried mainly by the neighbours.
